content:
sara: Heads up — after the RBAC refactor merged this morning, I can enumerate project namespaces from another org's service account. Not sure if read-only, but still not expected. Repro steps below.

matt: Yikes. Can you paste the exact commands?

sara: Yes — using the infra service account token:
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/orgs/123/projects
```
Response includes projects from org 456 as well. I filtered by org=123 but got 456 entries.

jenna: Is the policy evaluation incorrectly using `org_id` vs `workspace_id`? We changed evaluator to cache by user id earlier.

kyle: Rolling back the change on my end to test. Which commit?

sara: PR #892: rbac/evaluator: cache eviction change. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/892

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed rbac-refactor v2 to prod at 2026-03-20T09:05:12Z by matt

matt: I see. Can someone check audit logs for the request? If it's cross-org read we need to mark as sev2.

auditor-bot: audit-bot: Query results for request id abc-123:
```
{ "request_id": "abc-123", "actor": "infra-sa@example.com", "action": "list:projects", "org": "123", "result_count": 42, "note": "matched_policy: rbac/v2/cache" }
```

jenna: Also check KMS envelope keys — if logs are sent to S3 and cross-org IAM allowed, we need to revoke temporary creds.

kyle: I'm starting a quick rollback to rbac/evaluator@main~1. Will push a revert PR in 10m. If we revert, we should rotate the infra SA token just in case.

sara: :thumbsup: I can confirm reproduction stopped after reverting in staging. Need to run a full audit to know scope.

matt: Escalating to #incidents, creating incident ticket: INC-2026-042. Assigning to eng-security + infra. Jenna please own triage.

jenna: On it. Will gather: list of impacted orgs, earliest occurrence, all request_ids, and the PR diff. Also will check KMS key policy: `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/projects-audit-key`.

sara: Also note: the change touched the cache key format — we accidentally removed `org:` prefix when building cache keys. Patch idea:
```
- cacheKey := fmt.Sprintf("user:%d:projects", userID)
+ cacheKey := fmt.Sprintf("org:%d:user:%d:projects", orgID, userID)
```

kyle: Nice catch. That explains cross-org leakage. I'll open a PR to include org in key and add unit test.

matt: We should also add an automated fuzz test to ensure namespace isolation. Add e2e that asserts list calls only return matching org ids.

sara: I'll prepare the test vectors. For now, keep the revert in prod until PR lands. Audit: set retention to keep raw logs for 90 days and export to S3 path `s3://sec-incident-exports/INC-2026-042/` encrypted w/ projects-audit-key.

jenna: Noted. Also check KMS grants — remove any grants that allow cross-account decrypt. Will coordinate with security infra.

kyle: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/900 (fix cache key + tests). Requesting review from jenna and matt.

matt: Thanks. If we confirm no exfil beyond project names, document in sigsec notes. Otherwise escalate legal. I'll update the incident ticket.
